prompt: Complete NumberMath.sumOf so it totals any list of numbers -- List<Integer>, List<Double>, List<Long> -- using an upper-bounded wildcard and doubleValue().
explanation: List<Integer> is NOT a subtype of List<Number>, so a plain List<Number> parameter would reject it. The upper-bounded wildcard List<? extends Number> accepts a list of Number or any of its subtypes, which is exactly what a read-only consumer of numbers needs. Every Number provides doubleValue(), giving a uniform way to accumulate the total as a double.
hints: Loop over the list with an enhanced for loop typed as Number: for (Number n : nums).
Each element, whatever its concrete type, supports n.doubleValue().
Start a double accumulator at 0.0 and add each converted value to it.
